### rule_compute_equivalence
Scratch sweep (`/tmp/audit_pharmacy_fills_and_renewals_0081`, normalised whitespace): every `compute_basis` value is verbatim in its policy's `rule` (5/5 policies, 0 misses); every `baseline.rule` sentence is in the `rule`; every `prerequisite.policy_source` is in the blocked policy's `rule`. One compute binding without a `compute_basis` key: `ship_net` in rx_ext_shipping_overcharge_refund (its sentence "The net shipping line … plus every refund line pointing at that shipping line" is quoted under ship_posted/ship_refunded) — observation O-1.
Sentence-by-sentence sweep back (all five policies):
- shipment selection "the prescription's latest dispensed fill, latest by fill_date" ↔ `LATEST('rx_fills','rx_fill_id', date_field='fill_date', event_type='rx_fill_dispensed')`; reships/returns excluded by event_type. Same-day ties between two dispensed fills of one prescription are impossible under base rx_refill_timing (minimum elapsed share > 0), so no tie rule is needed for this read.
- shipping line "the latest shipping charge line pointing at that fill" ↔ LATEST rx_shipping_charged rx_fill_id=fid; base S7 "Shipping is charged once per dispensed fill" + owed-shipping's "no shipping line" scope keep it single.
- net shipping line ↔ ship_posted + SUM refunds original_charge_id=ship_line. ✓
- benefit line "latest fill charge line posted on that basis, latest by charge_date" ↔ LATEST rx_fill_charged price_basis=pbm_patient_pay. ✓ (but see POL-3: one line selected while the waiting sentence quantifies over every line)
- collected "every fill charge line and shipping charge line pointing at the dispensed fill plus every refund line pointing at that fill" ↔ SUM all rx_charges rx_fill_id=fid. ✓ (refund lines carry the original's rx_fill_id in every tool body)
- drug allowed: cash_price_90_day for a 90-day fill else 30-day, less member percent, rounded half up ↔ `RND(cash*(100-mb_pct)/100+1e-9,2)`. The K constants pct_* equal the charter's member_discount_pct_by_membership_tier for Value/Core (30/20/10), Extended (25/15/10), Specialty (15/10/5); brands → 0 = charter. ✓
- benefit drug allowed "lesser of the pbm patient pay recorded on the line and the member cash price" ↔ `MN(pbm, member_cash)`. ✓
- speed fee / Premier waiver / peak / weekend / 90-day / protection ladders: every tier stated in prose and implemented one-to-one (weekday via DAYS from Monday 2024-01-01 mod 7: 3=Thu, 4=Fri; peak by ISO string compare, inclusive). ✓
- "not above zero → nothing / no line" ↔ `MX(0.0, …)` then RND; owed shipping "or a shipping line already points at the fill" ↔ `ship_lines == 0` in in_scope. ✓
- rounding: RND(x+1e-9,2) on non-negative values; coordinator ruling (DSL-KNOWN) applies. Rule says drug price rounded, then final difference rounded — matches compute order. ✓
- B1 probes (absent membership → CFIELD None → 0% / full speed fee = "every other patient"; absent fill → in_scope False → 0; 0.00 fee → no line; negative difference → nothing) — words and compute agree.
- Undeclared tiered sentences: rx_ext_benefit_line_refund carries the peak-season sentence in rule and compute but no `peak_season_surcharge` factor; rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment and rx_ext_cash_shipment_refund carry the 90-day sentence but no `ninety_day_parcel` factor. They are rule-and-compute consistent; they are simply not counted as factors (observation O-2).

### prerequisite_sentences
1. balance ← overcharge refund: "The shipment balance is fixed only after the shipment's shipping line, plus every refund line pointing at it, stands no higher than the shipping fee the shipment balance allows." Connective "only after"; waits on a record-visible state (shipping line + refunds on it vs the allowed fee); no tool / id / snake_case. Writes of this difficulty that can lower a shipping line's net: only `refund_rx_shipping_overcharge_36ef431c` (the two other refund tools accept only rx_fill_charged lines; the balance and owed-shipping tools add charges). Derivation: sentence → state false when net shipping > allowed → the policy whose rule refunds a shipping line "posted above the shipping schedule … on its own line" for a cash-member-price shipment → rx_ext_shipping_overcharge_refund. Single reading. Not restated in the overcharge rule. ✓
2. balance ← benefit-line refund: "The shipment balance is not collected until every fill charge line of the same prescription posted on the pharmacy-benefit basis above the lesser of its recorded pbm patient pay and its member cash price carries a billing-error refund." Connective "not … until"; state form; the writing policy is the one whose rule re-prices "a fill charge line posted on the pharmacy-benefit basis" by a billing-error refund → rx_ext_benefit_line_refund. Single reading. "its member cash price" is defined only in the benefit-line rule (the balance rule names "the drug charge the shipment balance allows", the same formula) — observation O-5. But the sentence quantifies over every such line while its resolver prices one line and nets the whole shipment — see POL-3.
3. cash refund ← owed shipping: "The cash shipment refund is worked out only after the shipment's records carry a shipping line for the dispensed fill whenever the shipping fee the cash shipment refund allows is above zero." Connective "only after"; state form with a de minimis carve-out ("whenever … above zero") stated in the sentence (XF D2 ✓). Only `pay_rx_owed_shipping_bbdf4b04` posts a shipping line in this difficulty. Its scope (cash_price basis, no shipping line) equals the waiting policy's scope, and it posts exactly the fee the waiting policy allows (same formulas) → satisfiable in every engaged world (D1 ✓).
- No rule states a cross-problem order that grounds no declared edge. No base sentence grounds an edge.

- S2 "A patient whose membership tier is in free_expedited_membership_tiers pays nothing for expedited shipping and pays shipping_overnight_fee less shipping_expedited_fee for overnight." — handled differently: every extended rule charges such a patient the waived/reduced speed fee **plus** peak, weekend, 90-day and protection amounts. rx_evt_fill_pricing (refs of balance, benefit-line, cash refund):

rx_returns_and_reships (refs of overcharge, benefit-line, cash refund):

- R6 "A refund may be issued only when no refund already points to the same line." — inherited; the extended rules compute net of earlier refunds on the same line, so a world with a prior refund on the target line would make extended and base disagree (checked per task: no prior refund on any target line in either world).

  - ninety_day_parcel — R6 candidate; **fails ladder reality (FAC-1)**: a 90-count tablet bottle ships in the same mailer as a 30-count; days supply is not a dimension a mail-order pharmacy or carrier weighs for an air-shipping fee, and mail-order pharmacies price 90-day supplies to *lower* per-fill shipping, not raise it.

### findings
- **POL-1 SOURCE-POLICY RED (C1 undeclared override; also fails R6 condition 3 for peak_season_surcharge, weekend_transit_fee, ninety_day_parcel, package_protection).** Symptom: two in-force clauses price a Premier member's expedited/overnight shipping differently. Root cause: base rx_evt_shipping S2 "A patient whose membership tier is in free_expedited_membership_tiers pays nothing for expedited shipping and pays shipping_overnight_fee less shipping_expedited_fee for overnight." is named in no `overwrite`, while every extended rule states "where that tier and one of those statuses hold … the speed fee … is 0.00 / shipping_overnight_fee less shipping_expedited_fee" **plus** "the surcharges and fees … each counted once". Evidence: rx.yaml rx_evt_shipping rule; rx.extended.yaml all five `overwrite` lists (only S1, R7, F1). Consequence (same situation, two conclusions): a Premier member's Friday-overnight 90-day fill allows 15.00 under S2 but 15.00+3.50+8.00+4.00+protection under the extended rules. Bears on task 0 (overcharge refund, benefit-line refund) and task 1 (owed shipping payment); demonstrated in each task file. Affected: rx.extended.yaml all five policies (overwrite lists, rule surcharge sentences).
- **POL-2 SOURCE-POLICY RED (C1 undeclared override of a parameter meaning).** Base parameter_schema `charge_timing: 'When fills and shipping are charged: at_shipment.'` and rx_evt_fill_pricing F1 vs rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment "Because the fee was not taken at shipment, the owed shipping payment is the patient's own payment … posted as one shipping charge line" — a shipping charge after shipment; rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment's `overwrite` names only rx_evt_shipping S1 and its base_policy_refs omit rx_evt_fill_pricing. Second reading: under the in-force at-shipment timing a shipping fee not taken at shipment is not charged later → no owed-shipping write. Bears on task 1 (demonstrated there). Affected: rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment overwrite/base_policy_refs.
- **POL-3 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF D1 — waiting state not satisfiable by its resolver in every engaged world).** The balance's waiting sentence requires "every fill charge line of the same prescription posted on the pharmacy-benefit basis above the lesser of its recorded pbm patient pay and its member cash price carries a billing-error refund", but (a) rx_ext_benefit_line_refund prices only "the prescription's latest fill charge line posted on that basis" — with two such lines the earlier can never receive its refund; and (b) the resolver nets the whole shipment ("collected less the total … allows; when that difference is not above zero nothing is refunded and no line is written") — a benefit line above the lesser on a shipment whose shipping was under-collected (e.g. Extended 90-day, pbm 70.00 vs member cash 63.00, Premier Thursday-expedited 90-day with no shipping line: collected 70.00, allowed 63.00+7.95 → no refund line) never carries a refund. In either world the balance can never be collected, though its rule says the shortfall "is settled by a balance charge". Charter-global; not engaged in task 0's world (one benefit line; its refund is positive). Affected: rx_ext_cash_shipment_balance prerequisite sentence vs rx_ext_benefit_line_refund selection/netting.
- **POL-4 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF A9 + B2 — membership read has no selection rule and no as-of date).** Every ladder reading membership says "the tier on the patient's membership record" / "the patient's membership on the records" (no date), whereas base rx_evt_fill_pricing/rx_evt_shipping grant the discount/waiver "while" the status holds (at the charge). The compute reads `CFIELD('membership', …)`, which returns the first listed holding (check_compute.py `CFIELD` → `hs[0]`) — "first listed" is a rejected selection rule (B7). Decoy probe: a cancelled membership listed before a current one, or a tier changed between the fill_date and today, gives two readings. Not engaged in either task world (one membership each, unchanged since before every fill). Affected: member_percent and premier_speed_waiver ladders in all five policies.
- **POL-5 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF C2 — shared overwrite names no scope and dangles).** The S1 `replaced_by` ("… together with the Larkspur Pharmacy shipping surcharges stated in this rule for the fill's records, each counted once") names no scope and, substituted into rx_evt_shipping, refers to surcharges "stated in this rule" where that rule states none; shipments outside every extended scope (e.g. a standard-basis cash_price shipment with its shipping line posted) get either the surcharges (read from the extended rules) or none (read from the base rule). No consequence in either task world (both in scope). Affected: S1 overwrite entries of all five policies.
- **FAC-1 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (unreal ladder — realism_bar X5 / ladder-reality test; R6 condition 2 fails).** weekend_transit_fee (all five) and ninety_day_parcel (overcharge, balance, benefit-line) select fees on conditions a US mail-order pharmacy does not weigh for a shipping charge (see factor_ladders realism grading). With both struck, rx_ext_shipping_overcharge_refund keeps 3 factors, rx_ext_benefit_line_refund 3, rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment 3 — below the 4-factor floor; balance (4) and cash refund (4) stay at the floor. Bears on task 0 (both factors engaged) and task 1 (weekend engaged). Per-task weight demonstrations in the task files.
- Observations: O-1 `ship_net` has no compute_basis key; O-2 tiered sentences not declared as factors (peak in benefit-line; 90-day in owed shipping and cash refund); O-3 state_gate `gate` names a field; O-4 balance←overcharge `effect` overstates the rise under the MX floor; O-5 "its member cash price" defined only in the benefit-line rule; O-6 premier_speed_waiver method label accepted under A6; O-7 package_protection keyed on posted (possibly erroneous) fill charges.

## post_freeze_addendum (written after both task derivations were frozen and GT revealed; the charter_global_frozen section above is unchanged)
- Scope partition confirmed against `charter_scope`: task 0 {rx_ext_benefit_line_refund, rx_ext_shipping_overcharge_refund, rx_ext_cash_shipment_balance}; task 1 {rx_ext_owed_shipping_payment, rx_ext_cash_shipment_refund} — pairwise disjoint over whole trees, jointly complete over the five extended policies.
- R6 condition 6 check (worklog.md, read after the freeze): the worklog's Step 0 records the four surcharges as "a Larkspur Pharmacy published shipping surcharge schedule (R1, keyed on recorded keys …)" and calls them "the only invented figures"; no factor carries an `R6` tag with a per-factor reason.
- **FAC-2 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (AMENDMENT 1 — invented figures dressed as R1; R6 conditions 3 and 6 fail).** peak_season_surcharge, weekend_transit_fee, ninety_day_parcel and package_protection are not in the frozen rx charter (parameter_schema has no surcharge key; rx_evt_shipping prices only the three speed fees and the Premier waiver), so they are R6 by AMENDMENT 1's definition ("a Larkspur published schedule figure"), yet they are recorded as R1 and untagged (condition 6), and they conflict with the in-force base S2 for Premier members without a declared overwrite (condition 3, POL-1). AMENDMENT 1: "A factor dressed as R1–R5 that is in fact invented is RED (X5 / X6)" and "An R6 factor that fails any condition is RED under the condition it fails." peak_season_surcharge and package_protection would otherwise be plausible R6 figures; weekend_transit_fee and ninety_day_parcel additionally fail condition 2 (FAC-1). Consequence for counts: with the four struck, every policy keeps only member_percent and/or premier_speed_waiver (overcharge 1, owed shipping 1, balance 2, benefit-line 2, cash refund 2) — far below the 4-factor floor; the worklog's own Step 0 records that the rx base gives each line at most two real price levers. Bears on both tasks (demonstrated in 0.md / 1.md findings).
- Worklog "Known audit-facing risks: … netted shipment settlements make some shipping factors bear weight through netting (mechanically load-bearing)" — confirmed in both task files (shipping factors cancel across the prerequisite and the root under a consistent solve; recorded as observations, since the single-substitution test passes).
